purpose: Bounded offline exploration of execution-residual neural anti-windup, not formal validation
hypothesis: Pure normal-rate projection can leave useful compensation requests inconsistent with their admitted modal force. A bounded fixed-feature weight correction toward admitted prediction may reduce this mismatch without changing the actuator allocator.
eligibility: CA only; pure-rate cause; no amplitude, speed, withdrawal or contraction; effective sector*gate>=0.1; useful post-gradient prediction and non-adverse achieved prediction. Accepted original repair cycles excluded.
fixedBaseline: exact S3R2, default2-count/ms slew and all original hard guards
finiteScreen: Six candidates, existing36 assumed plants; all outputs retained. No iterative parameter search based on the first favourable case.
decision: Reject release if there are new completed-case failures or no mean synchronization benefit against R2. Tracking cost and ordinary-BLNN comparison are reported, not hidden. A positive screen is only exploration in uncalibrated models, not hardware efficacy or a tracking-tolerance justification.
localProperty: At fixed features and execution target, accepted projected correction cannot increase prediction-target distance or reverse a useful prediction. This is not full closed-loop stability.
